sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: PCT Patent Application and International Trademark Registration

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Federal common law; Quebec private law is civil law based on the Civil Code of Quebec)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Canada-China Agreement for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (S.C. 2000, c. 17) (PCMLTFA) and related Regulations; Quebec Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1); Quebec Civil Code, Book 4 (Limited Partnership); FINTRAC Guidance on client identification, KYC and record keeping; Canada's Accessible Patent Prosecution Agency regime under the Patent Act; applicable provincial professional licensing rules (patent and trademark agents governed by the Colleges of Patent Agents and Trademark Agents under federal legislation); Quebec Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency (for corporate general/limited partners, issued by home registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home jurisdiction corporate registry or registered agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of constitutional documents (charter, articles, bylaws) for corporate partners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicable corporate registry or competent official (Secretary of State/Registered Agent)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Individual partner's passport and proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority and local municipal/utility authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney authorizing the Quebec resident agent to file the declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in partner's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming partner identity and financial standing

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all prospective partners, beneficial owners, general partner, and persons with significant control against Canadian OFSI (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions) consolidated sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions lists, EU sanctions, OFAC SDN list, and Quebec Ministry of Public Security anti-money-laundering directives; enhanced due diligence for any Politically Exposed Person (PEP), foreign PEP, or family/close associate; compliance with the 'Know Your Client' rules of FINTRAC under the PCMLTFA; verification of professional licenses of prospective patent and trademark agents.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), online portal 'CliquezAffaires' (cliquezaffaires.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be exclusively French unless a statutory exemption applies; trade names must be in French for inscription in the register; English names or transliterations may be used only where the enterprise qualifies for an exception under the Charter of the French Language, and where required the name must be accompanied by a French version that is the primary displayed name; acronyms, initials, and phonetic variations are assessed against the avoidance of confusion with existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In case of name rejection, the applicant may within 15 days file an administrative review with the Quebec Enterprise Registrar by submitting Form 'Demande de révision d'une décision du registraire' through CliquezAffaires, outlining the distinctiveness and conformity with the Charter of the French Language; if the review is denied, the applicant may bring a judicial appeal before the Court of Québec within 30 days of the notification; the enterprise must refrain from conducting any business under a rejected or confusing name; new reservations are allowed after expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is generally not permissible for a Quebec statutory limited partnership; the office must be a physical address in Quebec where records are kept, where notices and process may be served, and where the LP's general partner maintains its activities; a serviced office (non-tenant used only for registration) may be subject to challenge; a physical meeting place for the general partner is strongly recommended for creditors and regulators.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspections is assessed at 15% since the registrant belongs to a regulated professional services activity (patent prosecution agency) subject to provincial and federal oversight, but not a high-risk financial activity; FINTRAC inspections may occur on a risk-based basis; the probability of an inspection in the first 12 months is moderate-low.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and reservation fee with the Quebec Registrar
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registraire des entreprises (Revenu Québec/Gouvernement du Québec)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the limited partnership declaration (declaration initiale)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Quebec Enterprise Registration Regulations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille of partner identification bundle (two corporate partners and one individual general partner)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Home jurisdiction notary and competent authority (e.g., provincial authentication service)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (approx. CAD 80 per authentication; notary fees vary)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government administrative fee for apostille processing (multiple documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Provincial authentication authority (e.g., Alberta or Ontario official documents service)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per applicable provincial apostille regulation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence and drafting of the limited partnership agreement (Quebec civil law), including KYC/UBO verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for cross-border LP establishment and corporate due diligence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of the declaration with the Revenu Québec (taxation ID) and registration for SGI (information return)
Professional licensing application review for patent prosecution agency (Patent Agent/Attorney registration pre-clearance)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: College of Patent Agents and Trademark Agents (Government of Canada)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee per federal Patent Agent Regulations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Translation and apostilled French legalization of partner documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator (OQLC recognized) and notary office

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency reserve for regulatory follow-up and sanctions/KYC screening tools

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), arts. 2236-2266 (société en commandite) and Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), ss. 9-12 and 24-28
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), an integrated registry under the Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation — Déclaration de société en commandite / Limited Partnership Declaration of Registration
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital under the Civil Code of Québec; partners must contribute the amounts fixed in the limited partnership agreement, and all contributions must be recorded in the partnership register; no government escrow account is required by law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS the general partner(s) of [●] L.P. have received the subscription schedule for capital contributions from the limited partners and determined that the initial capital is fully subscribed; RESOLVED: (1) The capital subscription schedule is adopted, and each limited partner’s obligation to fund a contribution is recorded in the partnership ledger. (2) The registered office of the limited partnership is established at [address], Province of Quebec, with the occupant’s consent. (3) [Name] is appointed managing partner with full authority to open banking accounts, execute patent prosecution retainers, and file statutory declarations. (4) The managing partner shall ensure registration of the declaration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and effect all corporate filings. This resolution is effective upon the Registrar’s issuance of the certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and legal form clearance for the Québec limited partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Dénominations (online service Éspace communicant)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request providing up to three proposed distinctive names, each with the mandatory legal element 'Limited Partnership / Société en commandite' or 'L.P. / S.E.C.'. The Registrar verifies the requested name against the enterprise register for confusion and restricts the use of any prohibited term. If a proposed name contains 'Canada', coordinate prior approval with Corporations Canada.
required_dossiers: Name reservation request form
Mandate or power of attorney, if applicable
List of three proposed names
Written authority from limited partners to reserve the name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusion or misleading content, submit a revised name reservation in the same online folder or appeal the decision to the Court of Québec within 30 days; a fresh reservation may be filed without loss of priority if done within the refusal notice period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and authentication of the declaration of registration for a société en commandite
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary appointed by the parties (Chambre des notaires du Québec) or legal counsel authorized to attest signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the declaration of registration identifying the limited partnership's name, head office, general partners, limited partners, the maximum amount of their contributions, and the restrictive clauses on limited partner liability. Have the declaration signed and authenticated before a notary of Quebec, and annex the capital contribution schedule and consent of the head-office occupant. For any corporate general partner, append its enterprise register extract and board resolution.
required_dossiers: Partnership declaration or notarial deed of registration
Notarized consent to establishment of head office
Domicile and coordinates of every general and limited partner
Certified extract from the enterprise register for any corporate general partner
Board resolution or equivalent authority for corporate general partner signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire refuses the declaration because of missing or erroneous particulars, file a corrective declaration within 30 days under article 2241 CCQ; a notarial correction deed may supplement the original declaration with retroactive effect to the initial filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of declaration and payment of government duties to the Québec Enterprise Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Centre d'entreprises (Corporate registry filing counter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the authenticated declaration through the Éspace communicant, pay the registration duty (CAD 79) by credit card or electronic wire, and upload the notarial deed or certified counterpart. The Registrar assigns the Fichier central des entreprises number and validates the head-office address.
required_dossiers: Notarized declaration of registration
Name reservation receipt
Proof of payment of registration duty
Consent of occupant for registered office
Record of the limited partners' capital contribution schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire issues a notice of refusal or a 'decision to correct', file a supplementary declaration within the prescribed 30-day cure period; if the refusal persists, initiate judicial review before the Court of Québec under section 29 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of certificate of registration and establishment of statutory partnership register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Certification and post-registration service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the certificate of registration and NEQ from the online portal, maintain a statutory register at the head office containing the partnership agreement, changes of partners or capital, and minutes of partner resolutions. The managing partner must file any change of coordinates or partner status within 15 days.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration/attestation of the Registraire
NEQ notification letter
Statutory register of partners and capital contributions
Partnership agreement and any amendments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a certified copy of the certificate is not issued due to registry error, request 'copie certifiée conforme' with payment of the prescribed fee; any erroneous registered data is corrected by filing a declaration of correction, which takes effect from the date it is accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, payroll and commercial registration with Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec — Mon dossier d'entreprise portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the enterprise registration form (immatriculation fiscale) to obtain Québec Sales Tax (TVQ) registration, source deductions for employees under the QPP/QPIP and CNESST, and income tax information number. The managing partner must certify the banking coordinates and indicate the nature of the patent prosecution activity.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration and NEQ from Registraire
List of partners and their Quebec/Business numbers
Bank account confirmation
Signed mandate for the tax representative
Declaration of business activity (ISIC 7490 / NAICS 541199)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Revenu Québec returns an incomplete registration, supply missing proof within 30 days; an objection to a tax assessment following registration can be filed under section 93.1 of the Tax Administration Act (Québec).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Professional licensing, environmental and civil-defense authorization for patent prosecution activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Collège des agents de brevets et des agents de marques de commerce (Patent Agent College) jointly with the Canadian Intellectual Property Office; local fire safety inspector; municipal zoning department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for registration as a patent agent firm under the Patent Act (Canada) if offering public patent prosecution services, secure professional liability insurance, and obtain an occupancy permit from the local municipality after verifying zoning and building capacity. Register any disposal of small quantities of hazardous waste with MELCCFP if dry-process office activities generate such waste, and complete the fire-safety compliance inspection.
required_dossiers: Patent agent firm registration application to CIPO/College
Professional liability insurance certificate
Municipal zoning and occupancy permit
Fire-safety prevention plan and inspection checklist
CNESST occupational health registration and attestation
MELCCFP registration for hazardous waste generator, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A refusal of patent agent registration is appealable to the Federal Court under section 15 of the Patent Act; an environmental authorization refusal may be cured by a revised remedial action plan, and fire-safety deficiencies by compliance order with reinspection certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Collège des agents de brevets et des agents de marques de commerce (Patent and Trademark Agent College) in coordination with the Canadian Intellectual Property Office (CIPO)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration as a Firm or Patent Agent under the Patent Act, RSC 1985, c P-4, s. 5, and the Patent Agent Rules; municipal occupancy permit for the professional office

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) — Direction de l'autorisation des projets
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration/Declaration (Répertoire des déclarations de conformité) — full EIA report not required for a low-emission professional office/patent agency below the threshold for industrial installations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater to municipal sewer only, meeting municipal sewer-use by-law limits; VOC emissions below 30 t/year if no solvent-based printing is installed; hazardous waste limited to small quantities (< 5 kg/month) managed under the Règlement sur les matières dangereuses; office waste recycling per municipal by-law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certificate from the local inspector under Quebec Fire Safety Code (CQLR c B-1.1, r. 7); structural load and occupancy limits verified under the National Building Code of Canada; panic hardware, emergency exit lighting, and accessibility clearance; CNESST occupational health and safety attestation, first-aid equipment, and an emergency response plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA / Agence du revenu du Canada) — federal tax authority for GST/HST, federal income tax, and customs matters; portal: CRA My Business Account and GST/HST NETFILE. Revenu Québec — Quebec tax authority for QST, Quebec income tax, payroll contributions, and related filings; portal: Clic Revenu (Entreprises).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Quebec limited partnership must first obtain a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. It must then register with the CRA for a federal Business Number (BN) and, where the LP makes taxable supplies in Canada or otherwise elects, a GST/HST program account. Registration with Revenu Québec for QST is also required if the LP is not a small supplier or if it elects to register. Non-resident partners must provide foreign tax identification data and the LP must maintain a Canadian address and agent for service. Applications are filed through CRA Form RC1 and Revenu Québec electronic registration; certified partnership documents and proof of general partner authority are generally required for foreign-controlled LPs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not apply a U.S.-style check-the-box regime; the CRA classifies a limited partnership as a flow-through entity. Available elections include voluntary GST/HST and QST registration before the mandatory threshold, non-calendar-year partnership fiscal period elections under ITA s.249.1, functional-currency reporting elections under ITA s.261, and elections to have non-resident partners compute certain Canadian-source income on an elective basis. Hybrid mismatch arrangements are addressed by mandatory adjustments under ITA ss.18.2 and 18.3 rather than by elective classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) and Quebec Sales Tax (QST); consumption-tax systems administered respectively by the CRA and Revenu Québec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies in a calendar quarter and preceding four calendar quarters for GST/HST small-supplier status; the same CAD 30,000 threshold applies for QST small-supplier status in Quebec. A Quebec LP carrying on commercial activity must nonetheless obtain the NEQ and register for GST/HST/QST if any threshold is exceeded or if it elects to register.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not currently impose real-time fiscal clearance, government pre-approval, or digital stamping of invoices. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically above prescribed revenue thresholds, and QST returns must be filed in accordance with Revenu Québec electronic filing requirements. Pan-Canadian electronic invoicing is voluntary and no API clearance or transaction-control stamping is mandatory for a patent prosecution agency.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Granted under Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act and corresponding QST rules where a supply is made to a non-resident who is not registered under GST/HST or QST, the service is not performed in connection with real property situated in Canada, is not in respect of tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of supply, and otherwise qualifies as a zero-rated service to a non-resident. Services rendered by a patent prosecution agency for foreign patent or trademark prosecution before foreign intellectual-property offices may be zero-rated where the recipient is non-resident, the work product is delivered abroad, and use of the service occurs outside Canada. A tax invoice must clearly indicate the zero-rated nature of the supply and the applicable statutory provision.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A) where physical priority documents, drawings, or other tangible items are exported; for pure services, the export contract and non-resident certification serve as the export record
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill, required only when physical goods or documents move across borders
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank-issued SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt of foreign-currency consideration and repatriation of export proceeds
Non-Resident Client Declaration with supporting proof of foreign residence, permanent establishment address, and non-registration status
Detailed zero-rated invoice, statement of work, and service completion report referencing the patent application or trademark registration matter
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess claimed export zero-rating, claw back any input tax credits or refunds, and impose unremitted GST/HST and QST with interest if the documentation does not establish a bona fide export to a non-resident. Penalties include late-remittance penalties under ETA s.280 equal to 5% plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months, gross-negligence and false-statement penalties under ETA s.285 of up to 25% of the amount at issue, and the same or substantially similar penalties under Quebec QST legislation. Fraudulent zero-rating claims may additionally attract criminal tax-evasion fines and imprisonment, and the limitation period for reassessment is extended where misrepresentation or wilful default is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the central monetary and settlement authority; prudential supervision of deposit-taking institutions by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); cross-border capital-movement, sanctions and export-control authority under the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA), the Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act and the United Nations Act, administered by Global Affairs Canada; anti-money-laundering and terrorist-financing supervision by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA); Quebec corporate-registry and beneficial-ownership oversight by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada has no exchange-control statute: the Currency Act (RSC, 1985, c. C-52) establishes the Canadian dollar as legal tender but imposes no restrictions on holding, converting or transferring foreign currency; the CAD is fully convertible on both current and capital account, consistent with OECD Article VIII and CUSMA obligations. Profit and capital remittances are unrestricted in quantum and timing. The operative hurdles for a Quebec limited partnership ('société en commandite') are tax-driven: a non-resident partner's allocable share of the partnership's Canadian-source business income is taxable under Part I of the Income Tax Act, and distributions to a non-resident partner attract Part XIII withholding under section 212.13 of the Income Tax Act at the 25% statutory rate, generally reduced to 5%-15% under an applicable tax treaty, with analogous provincial withholding exposure under the Taxation Act (Quebec) where income is sourced to a Quebec establishment. Bank-level practicalities are FINTRAC electronic-funds-transfer reporting for every international transfer of CAD 10,000 or more, FATCA/CRS account disclosure, and SEMA/UNA trade-control screening before any cross-border payment is released.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) to Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the limited partnership's fiscal year‑end (default: calendar year, i.e., due by March 1 of each year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 50 per occurrence; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers administrative strike‑off by REQ

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal year‑end (e.g., by May 31 for a December 31 year‑end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of CAD 50 per partner per day late, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500 per fiscal period

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit under Quebec's Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises for limited partnerships. Mandatory audit only if imposed by the LP agreement, a limited partner's statutory request (art. 2243 C.c.Q.), or a secured creditor's contractual covenant. For tax purposes, financial statements must be filed with the T5013 if the partnership has gross revenue or assets above CAD 1 million.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (for publicly accountable LPs) or Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for private LPs; the partnership must apply a consistent framework under Canadian GAAP

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec law does not impose a separate UBO annual confirmation for limited partnerships; however, the REQ must be updated within 30 days of any change to general partners (including name, address, and capacity). Limited partners are not required to be individually disclosed unless the partnership agreement or regulator so requires. Any transfer of partnership interest must be reflected in the partnership’s internal partner register and, where affecting general partner status, reported to REQ.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General Partners and Limited Partners (contributions, distributions, and transfers)
Minute Book / Resolutions of General Partners

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 4,000–8,000 for a review engagement; full audit 12,000–25,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 11.9% Quebec provincial corporate tax rate (2024), with federal rate of 15% on first $500,000 active business income and 38% thereafter
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction reducing federal effective rate to approximately 2.2% on first $500,000 of qualifying active business income from patent services; no provincial small business rate reduction for LPs

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T3 Partnership Return of Income (federal CRA) and equivalent provincial filing with Revenu Québec
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 90 days after fiscal year-end or June 15 following calendar year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate income from patent prosecution services before deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners report Canadian-source income only; no withholding on service fees unless treaty applies

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income from ISIC 7490 patent agency activities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Taxed at progressive individual rates or flat rate on Canadian source services; allocate share to non-resident partners

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty $50 per month (max $1,000); failure to file $100 minimum (max $25,000); underpayment interest 10-50% plus penalties

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on dividends from Canadian corporations to non-residents (reduced by applicable treaty)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Form NR301 to CRA with supporting TRC (Treaty Relief Certificate) to claim reduced rate; process via My Business Account portal
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties 10-25% (e.g. 10% US, 15% UK); interest 0-15% (e.g. 0% US under LOB provisions)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory threshold; mandatory documentation for related-party transactions exceeding $1 million or requested by CRA
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada lacks EU-style Economic Substance Regulations; GAAR applies to recharacterize arrangements lacking Canadian economic substance for non-resident controlled LPs

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or false statement in T3 return regarding patent service income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction with fines up to $100,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalties and interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners personally liable for restitution, fines, and potential imprisonment for willful evasion

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to document arm's length pricing for intercompany charges in patent prosecution services
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA adjustments to income, penalties up to 10% of transaction value, and interest on underpayments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners face personal liability for penalties, interest, and possible criminal charges

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Canadian LP with no Canadian management, employees, or operations used solely for non-resident tax avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income recharacterization, denial of treaty benefits, GAAR application, and potential criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners subject to civil restitution orders, fines up to $100,000, and imprisonment
